INSTRUMENTS.label: Shape
INSTRUMENTS.description: Scans a 2D contour with moving points, lines, or rays; each geometric contact shapes pitch, pan, level, and timbre.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, choose a reader, then move the contour or play a MIDI or computer key.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Solid
INSTRUMENTS.description: Cuts a moving 3D wireframe with a plane; every wire-plane intersection becomes a voice.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, choose a solid, then rotate it or move the cutting plane.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Möbius
INSTRUMENTS.description: Sweeps a two-dimensional plane through a half-twisted Möbius band, or runs a 16-station, two-lap counterpoint weave whose hocketed subject gains an offbeat answer and inverts on the shadow lap.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Choose Plane slice for playable intersection curves, or Counterpoint weave for the perpendicular A–B crossbar, mirrored pitch traces, and forward-only two-lap phrase.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Klein Bottle
INSTRUMENTS.description: Sweeps a two-dimensional plane through a figure-eight Klein bottle immersion while keeping coincident sheets separate in the parameter mesh.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on Audio, press Play or drag the 2D head, then tilt its plane and reshape the immersion while its glowing slice curves remain the score.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Hyper
INSTRUMENTS.description: Cuts a rotating 4D wireframe with a W hyperplane and sonifies the crossing edges.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, choose a 4D form, then move the W reader or start rotation.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Graph Synth
INSTRUMENTS.description: Sends inherited-pitch note pulses through editable directed graphs; edge length sets time, route turns set intervals, and cycle-closing edges create quieter, darker repeats.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, choose or generate a graph, then send one note or run the pulse clock while dragging nodes and switching routes.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Shapes
INSTRUMENTS.description: A self-contained Polygon, Polyhedra, and Hyperpolyhedra instrument with one canvas, one shared transport, and dimension-aware form and rotation controls.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Choose 2D, 3D, or 4D, then play the same running form continuously, as notes, or as triggers from the responsive Twin Rack panel.

INSTRUMENTS.label: L-Systems
INSTRUMENTS.description: A self-contained L-system instrument with one canvas, shared grammar controls, and Continuous, Notes, Triggers, and Mic playing modes.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Choose a grammar and mix preset, then keep the same branch traversal running while switching between sustained synth, note events, drum triggers, and live mic delay.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Graphs
INSTRUMENTS.description: A self-contained graph instrument with one editable network and Synth, Drums, and Mic playing modes that share its nodes, routes, motion, and timing.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Choose or generate a graph, then reshape and play the same topology while switching between pitched pulses, percussion triggers, and live microphone delay.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Tiles
INSTRUMENTS.description: A self-contained lattice and spiral instrument with one canvas, shared isohedral tile controls, sustained synth modes, and FM drum trigger modes.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Choose Lattice, Lattice Drums, Spiral, or Spiral Drums, then keep the same tile form and reader transport running while switching sound engines.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Mazes
INSTRUMENTS.description: Carves orthogonal, radial, or hexagonal fields as paired passage-center and wall-outline voices, with a distinct visual and sonic process for each maze algorithm.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Choose a field and builder, replay its construction, then optionally trace, tour, or solve the finished topology.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Paths
INSTRUMENTS.description: Draws Gilbert, Hilbert, Gosper, Dragon, and seeded walking paths as continuous vector scores whose direction, curvature, hierarchy, and position shape sound.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Choose a generator, draw it through time, then trace the finished path with one or more sounding heads.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Lattice
INSTRUMENTS.description: Slides an editable isohedral tiling beneath a reader so every crossed edge becomes a polyphonic synth event.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, choose a tiling, then start the motion and move the reader.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Spiral
INSTRUMENTS.description: Warps an isohedral tiling into log-polar space and scans its radial and spiral edges for sound.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, choose a reader, then run or drag the warped lattice.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Lattice Drum Machine
INSTRUMENTS.description: Turns tiling-reader contacts into drum hits selected and retuned by edge class, orientation, height, and angle.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, choose a tiling and bank, then start the lattice motion.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Spiral Drum Machine
INSTRUMENTS.description: Turns contacts in a log-polar tiling into drum patterns that follow its radial and spiral geometry.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, choose a bank and reader, then run the spiral field.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Shape Drum Machine
INSTRUMENTS.description: Turns contour contacts and corner events into drum hits whose voices change with position, angle, and phase.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, choose a reader and drum bank, then move the contour through it.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Solid Drum Machine
INSTRUMENTS.description: Turns intersections between a cutting plane and a 3D wireframe into a changing drum pattern.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, choose a bank, then rotate the solid or move the plane.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Hyper Drum Machine
INSTRUMENTS.description: Turns 4D hyperplane intersections into drum hits selected by position and four-dimensional rotation.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, choose a bank, then move the W reader or start rotation.

INSTRUMENTS.label: L-System Drum Machine
INSTRUMENTS.description: Walks through recursive branch heads and maps depth, angle, generation, phase, and position to drums.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, choose a grammar and drum bank, then generate and play the tree.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Graph Drum Machine
INSTRUMENTS.description: Propagates percussion triggers through editable directed graphs, mapping node position, degree, route turn, path depth, and cycle pass to a shared sixteen-voice FM drum bank.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, choose a topology and drum style, then seed a pulse or run the clock; cyclic routes return later with reduced amplitude and tone.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Rattle Snake Skin
INSTRUMENTS.description: Paints notes, glissandi, rings, and parameter fields onto a looping time-frequency canvas powered by continuous percussion.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, choose a preset and paint tool, draw on the canvas, then start the loop.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Rubix Cube Sequencer
INSTRUMENTS.description: Offers five mutually exclusive banks: four sample-free drum kits read the two side faces, while 303 Acid reads only the upper face through its Classic or WebGPU engine; hidden stickers stay hard-silent.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Choose one bank or preset, then drag the cube or enable Random Twists; in WebGPU 303 mode, sticker row, column, edge, current face, and visibility reshape each acid step.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Sliding Puzzle
INSTRUMENTS.description: Reads a resizable 2 × 2 through 8 × 8 square or rectangular tile field as either a serial score or Rubix-style parallel rows, with four fixed home-row colors and one moving silent cell.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Choose Lines together or One tile, set independent rows and columns, then slide complete lines, rotate the rectangle, scramble, or let Solve unwind the exact move history.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Hocket Luigi
INSTRUMENTS.description: Distributes one composite rhythm across two, three, or four editable voices, with sourced structural studies, visible gaps and collisions, phase shifts, and direct pulse ownership.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, run the loom, then drag or tap pulses between colored rings; keep Preserve composite on to move ownership without changing the combined rhythm.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Hyper Rubix
INSTRUMENTS.description: Separates five instrument presets—color drums, resonant prisms, bit voices, WebGPU acid, and seed-shell rattles—from three playback views: one selected cell, four view-facing cells, or all 64, 216, or 512 distinct notes in an order-2, order-3, or order-4 tesseract boundary.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio and Play shape loop, then orbit, Fold W, or make manual quarter-turns: the view chooses the clocked stickers while transformed position, depth, neighbors, fault lines, displacement, and disorder reshape each note without resetting time or adding a separate motion synth.

INSTRUMENTS.label: WebGPU 303
INSTRUMENTS.description: Streams a WGSL compute-shader acid voice into Web Audio chunks as a separate GPU synthesis instrument.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Use a WebGPU-capable browser, turn on Audio, then shape the pattern, partials, filter, and chunk settings.

INSTRUMENTS.label: SIMD 303
INSTRUMENTS.description: Expands the WebGPU 303 acid model with 512 band-limited partials, harmonic spectrum shaping, per-step expression, chorus, and delay inside a 128-frame AudioWorklet.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on Audio, press Play synth, shape the pattern and effects, or save named patches to My presets in this browser.

INSTRUMENTS.label: SIMD SYNTH
INSTRUMENTS.description: Combines two of eight synthesis models through selectable blend, ring, phase, shaping, filter-routing, modulation, and dual-effects stages in an eight-voice AudioWorklet.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on Audio, choose a signal-path preset, play the stage or MIDI keys, then swap sources and processing stages without patching cables.

INSTRUMENTS.label: WebGPU Chiptune
INSTRUMENTS.description: Translates srtuss's 2015 Shadertoy Chiptune sound shader into a live WGSL score with chip voices, drums, noise, and eight-tap ping-pong echo.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Use a WebGPU-capable browser, start the tracker, turn on Audio to hear it, then drag the score to reshape its deterministic seed and pitch range or open the full active-path controls.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Jaw Jam
INSTRUMENTS.description: Sequences one physical jaw-harp reed through plucks, pitch-inheriting sustains, and exact hard rests while every step can reshape material, mouth vowel, tine pull, breath power, and breath speed.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Choose a performance, drag each pluck block vertically for pitch, set its vowel and physical voice, balance PULL with AIR, then run independent pluck and breath clocks at ratios from one breath every three beats through three per beat.

INSTRUMENTS.label: GPU Shader Synths
INSTRUMENTS.description: Runs four control lanes, six adjustable synthesis models, editable additive ranks, a causal FIR, feed-forward delay taps, and waveshaping across two WGSL compute passes.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Use a WebGPU-capable browser, turn on Audio, choose a theme or sequence generator, then draw pitch, pulse, timbre, and model motion directly on the stage.

INSTRUMENTS.label: srtuss Master
INSTRUMENTS.description: Splits eight Shadertoy Sound programs into 48 selectable source parts while retaining all ten verified translations as exact Original programs.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Use a WebGPU-capable browser, start transport and Audio independently, choose a Parts preset or Explode mix, then shape, solo, mute, pan, or retime each voice card.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Modular Shader Synth
INSTRUMENTS.description: Patches typed synthesis, modulation, shaping, control, and spatial modules into an editable graph that renders stereo audio with WGSL compute shaders.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Use a WebGPU-capable browser, select a patch, turn on Audio, then select modules to change their parameters and signal routing.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Throatazoid
INSTRUMENTS.description: Feeds microphone input, an internal glottis, or both through up to seven editable vocal tracts.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Choose the glottis or microphone source, turn on audio, then drag the tongue and tract controls.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Pink Trombonazoid
INSTRUMENTS.description: Turns a written word into editable phoneme blocks and automation lanes that animate pitch, breath, tongue, lips, nasal coupling, and mutation through a physical vocal tract.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Enter a word, turn on audio, press Say word, then reshape its phoneme timing and articulatory automation lanes.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Throat Singing
INSTRUMENTS.description: Keeps a pressure-driven glottal drone and a tract-selected upper melody inside one 44-section airway, with two constrictions, converging F2/F3 resonances, and optional ventricular-fold period division.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, choose a Tuvan style or comparison preset, then retune the drone with A S D F G H J K while selecting harmonics or dragging the tongue and pharynx controls.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Syrinx
INSTRUMENTS.description: Models mammal folds, paired bird labia, frog membranes, and a rodent jet whistle through species-bounded vocal anatomy.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Choose an animal and call, turn on audio, then trigger the gesture or hold Breath while reshaping its biological controls.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Tongued Beasts
INSTRUMENTS.description: Grafts human, macaque, canine, and avian tongue mechanics onto physical animal voice sources so tongue shape and motion continuously reshape the tract.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, choose a host animal and tongue entity, then drag the anatomy or trigger a tongue movement preset.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Hybrinx
INSTRUMENTS.description: Reveals the native keyframed pressure, pitch, closure, mouth, cavity, roughness, source-split, and bilateral-balance contours that animate physical animal calls through a playable tongue-shaped tract.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, choose a host beast and native call, then play or loop it while the live timeline traces every sounding parameter contour beneath the animal.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Creaturazoid
INSTRUMENTS.kind: Monophonic creature voice and body sequencer
INSTRUMENTS.description: Routes 50 gestures—36 animal voices plus 14 procedural hisses, impacts, scrapes, wing sounds, breaths, feeding clicks, and locomotion—through one persistent absolute Hybrinx body.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, choose a persistent body and rhythm, then intersperse vocal calls with body percussion; every rectangular step retargets the same airway and body-cavity resonator.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Quadruped
INSTRUMENTS.description: Keeps species-shaped bodies, including Frog, above a compact sixteen-card motion study; touchdown, load, push, support, lift-off, and landing share one exact global BPM clock with three optional melodic calls.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Play Solo, Herd or Trio and edit each animal's foot and call score. Borrow the same gait dictionary and stretch leaps or skids. Change continuous ground material or stair direction for seeded friction and depth color; tempo stays independent.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Roach Synth
INSTRUMENTS.description: A grounded cockroach scan with 31 playable joints, static poses and 24 varied motions, a body-part mixer, real movement recordings and a crunchy word voice.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn Audio on, play a held pose or animate it, then mix its legs, shell, wings and voice. Drag a body part, choose a motion, or make a new random motion.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Spider Synth
INSTRUMENTS.description: A detailed orb-weaver scan with eight articulated legs in a playable web. Leg contacts pluck silk subdivisions, while held poses, a body mixer and a tiny voice shape its sound.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn Audio on, pluck a strand or animate the spider. Drag its joints, move it across the web, change silk tension, or hold MIDI keys to play temporary poses.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Monstrozoid
INSTRUMENTS.description: Routes variable lungs, vocal-fold sources, paths, and mouth resonators through continuous pressure, tension, routing, articulation, impact, and resonance contours.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio and select a call to hear it immediately, or start continuous flow; then edit anatomy counts, route connections, vocal behavior, and modulation contours.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Blowhole
INSTRUMENTS.description: Separates delphinid phonic lips, the sperm whale's right-sided spermaceti pathway, and the coupled U-fold/cricoid-cushion source of baleen-whale song while the external blowhole remains a valve rather than the underwater sound source.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, choose a dolphin or whale call, then play its visible gesture or hold pressure while dragging the paired source, air sac, and radiator anatomy.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Jaw Harp
INSTRUMENTS.description: Couples a plucked cantilever reed to an interactive mouth cavity so one fixed reed fundamental excites harmonics selected by the tongue, jaw, lips, and cavity.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, choose a harp and vowel preset, then pull and release the copper trigger or press Space to pluck.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Harmonicazoid
INSTRUMENTS.description: Models a three-octave, ten-hole diatonic harmonica as paired blow and draw reeds, with independent keys and reed bodies, one- to five-hole apertures, bends, tongue blocks, a moving hand-cavity resonance, and signed blues breath rhythms.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, choose Midnight Growl or another performance, then hold Blow or Draw; pull either lip-window edge, reshape the tongue and bend, sweep the hand cup, or move Breath Shift from pristine to sloppy.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Julie Saw
INSTRUMENTS.description: Localizes a long singing mode at the inflection of an S-curved steel blade, then couples bow pressure, signed speed, rosin, and moving contact through a velocity-weakening stick–slip junction.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, drag Julie's pink flex hand to bend and curl the blade, then drag the amber bow across its moving sweet spot. Lift to ring, or explore sourced bow pulses, vibrato, glides, mallets, edge pluck, scrape, and choke.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Hiccup Head
INSTRUMENTS.description: Moves a softly translucent, step-shifting pastel-rainbow checkerboard polka-dot goofball face and one persistent Pink Trombone–lineage oral waveguide between fifty-two exclusive gestures, including sustained alveolar ZZZZ, a vibrato-rich EH-YEAH vowel carousel, moving WAOW, arched WHOOP, pitched DOO-DOO, held lateral LLLL, long RRRR, alternating L-R-L-R, LA-LA-LA, four-place KLIK-KLAK clicks, low PURR, warm HUFF, short HIC!, full HICCUP!, EEF! breaths, a wet double KISS, bidirectional BRUSH tooth gliss, mouth KSH snare, longer cheek toms, BRRAP, resonant face claps, open-throat and rough voices, grunt, moan, PB-PB, a wet pull-out tongue, missing-incisor FWEE, and twelve pitched dead-wood teeth.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Tap any of fifty-two feature-clear sound dots, the whistle gap, or twelve separately pitched crooked teeth. Choose or mutate among seven contrasting physical sound banks; every bank retunes the same monophonic mouth and auditions its result. KISS leaves a fading lip print at a changing face position, BRUSH sends a visible toothbrush up and down while sweeping both directions across the wood-toned teeth, and blue slap mitts appear only while SLAP or SMACK is dragged. Pull either horizontal-tethered ear for stereo width, and drag each straight side-hair tip in two dimensions—length sets echo amount while angle sets that side's delay time. Matched circular eyes move inward for bright plate reverb, outward for a dark cathedral, and downward to thicken the room; centered open eyes are dry. Use two thick eyebrows as a cyclic sequence-amplitude contour. The large glossy #FF0000 circular nose controls the nasal branch, while the oval green, translucent-striped lips become thinner as the mouth opens. Persistent Delay, Reverb, Nasal, and Stereo switches and live amounts stay put through preset changes, mutation, and reset. Sequence one gesture per column at any length from 1 through 64 steps and up to 520 BPM, then edit or mutate one to eight sequential voice characters—including direct vibrato rate and depth—without layering mouths.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Digestazoid
INSTRUMENTS.description: Couples a compliant stomach, peristaltic intestinal and colon chambers, gas, bile-like liquid, viscous sludge, a finite bubble-cloud model, and pressure-driven upper and lower tissue valves into one persistent wet body. Bubble events pass through dirty nucleation, submerged inverse-size rings, neck pinch, surface rupture, viscous glugs, and shared low abdominal modes.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, push and prod the cutaway organs, hold Inflate or Deflate, pinch and release a valve, pull the lower rubber outlet, or play growl, clustered burble, bubble rupture, slosh, burp, sludge burple, and short or sustained fart gestures.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Mouthophones
INSTRUMENTS.description: Mouthophones compares nineteen breath-driven and mouth-resonated instruments through six physical source topologies, from quill-driven strings and bidirectional free reeds to lip reeds, edge-tone flutes, lamellophones, and mouth bows.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Choose an instrument by evidence tier, turn on audio, then hold inhale or exhale; for hand-driven strings, pluck, rub, or bow against a linked breath rhythm.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Spelling Synthesizer
INSTRUMENTS.description: Sounds each typed letter through the Bellazoid tract, sustained KAL phone samples, or the twenty-band Voxazoid vocoder while typing rhythm shapes the voice.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Begin typing, choose an engine and personality, then adjust rhythm dynamics and the vowel-pair delay.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Vocalzoid
INSTRUMENTS.description: Turns one written word into editable pitched notes, sustained vowel bodies, and overlapped phoneme joins using bundled open sample voices or a local UTAU bank.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, drag the syllable notes into a melody, choose KAL16 or one of eight bundled open demo voices, then press Sing word; extracted UTAU folders can be imported locally.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Lumber Loops
INSTRUMENTS.description: Records microphone loops as playable rings with pitch handles, filters, direction, pan, mute, solo, and shared delay.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Allow microphone access, record a first ring, then drag its playheads and pitch handles.

INSTRUMENTS.label: L-system Delay
INSTRUMENTS.description: Runs live microphone audio through an L-system tree where branches become delays and turns become pitch shifts.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Allow microphone access, start input, then change the grammar or branch timing.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Graph Delay
INSTRUMENTS.description: Routes live microphone audio through a generated delay graph with switchable paths, pitch shifts, and feedback.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Allow microphone access, choose a graph preset, then start input and open or close routes.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Micromorph
INSTRUMENTS.description: Streams microphone audio and sample-clocked performance controls to an optional local diffusion model, while five visible membranes expose the path from source to imaginary descendant.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Use headphones, turn on the microphone, move Ancestor distance through the five derivation stages, then connect an MGA Stream v1 model host for neural audio; without one, the page identifies its bounded rehearsal DSP honestly.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Shepard–Risset
INSTRUMENTS.description: Builds the illusion of endlessly rising or falling pitch from overlapping octave layers.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, choose a direction or preset, then adjust speed, density, and range.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Slippery Resynthesis
INSTRUMENTS.description: Tracks microphone or local-file audio across logarithmic FFT bands, then rebuilds it through endlessly slipping Shepard glissando banks with adaptive consonant excitation.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Choose Mic or File, turn on audio, then shape the glide, transpose, spectral tilt, carrier color, consonant detail, stereo spread, and dry/slip mix.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Drum Roll Please!
INSTRUMENTS.description: Translates the Shepard–Risset illusion into overlapping tempo octaves whose struck voices morph from kick through tom, hand drum, and air.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Choose a direction and tempo glissando, then optionally make pitch follow the endlessly changing rhythm rate.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Ouroborousel
INSTRUMENTS.description: Builds an endless roll from higher-note chunks, Ouroboros drum bodies, or both, carrying octave-related pulses through the rhythm–pitch fusion threshold.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Choose Notes, Ouroboros Drums, or Notes + Drums, start the carousel, and shape its direction, roll rate, bank width, and shared rhythm-to-pitch fusion; Notes and Combo also expose note-chunk controls.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Ourorourobouroboros
INSTRUMENTS.description: Purple-and-blue octave rings carry slow drum or note rhythms into pitch, then slower phase-locked gates carve silences into the high spectrum so the next rhythm seems to emerge from inside it.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Choose Notes, Drums, or Layered, add or remove Shepard rings, then shape the pitch threshold, note-lift/nested distance, interruption reach, silence depth, and rhythm-to-sustain audio mix.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Ouroboros
INSTRUMENTS.description: Strikes a Rattlesnake-style drum through octave-related Shepard bodies whose pitch keeps rising or falling while the audible register appears never to leave.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, choose Rise or Fall, then balance glissando speed, hit rate, octave-bank width, and the kick-to-air timbre morph.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Ouroboros Borealis
INSTRUMENTS.description: Crosses an endless Shepard pitch bank with an endless Risset rhythm bank, giving one Rattlesnake percussion body independent illusory pitch and tempo motion.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Start the dual playheads, send pitch and rhythm together or in opposite directions, then reshape their intervals, phase, coupling, ranges, and timbre.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Sandy Syrup Delay
INSTRUMENTS.description: Processes microphone or file audio with staggered grains that can hold their rates or glide together.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Choose microphone or a file, start the source, then move between Sand and Syrup behavior.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Candy Coil Delay
INSTRUMENTS.description: Uses staggered centered-hump delay heads that pass below, through, and above the source pitch.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Choose microphone or a file, start the source, then tap a range or lock its reciprocal relationship with head speed.

INSTRUMENTS.label: L-System
INSTRUMENTS.description: Expands turtle grammars into branching scores whose recursion, turns, taper, and timing shape a voice tree.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, select a grammar, generate the tree, then play its branch traversal.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Recursion
INSTRUMENTS.description: Runs noise, impulses, microphone capture, or a file through the recursive Fuzzy Donut signal process.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Choose a source, turn on audio, then raise the recursion depth and switch visual views.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Enveloper
INSTRUMENTS.description: Embeds three child envelopes inside one parent envelope, then divides them into nine FM notes with editable pitch and index contours; each ancestor segment's slope becomes inherited pitch glide.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio and start the tree clock, drag parent and child nodes to reshape time, level, and inherited bend, then set each leaf's base sound and its two modulation contours.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Julia
INSTRUMENTS.description: Traces a Julia-set boundary and maps left and right turns to cyclic Shepard pitch.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, choose or drag the Julia parameter, then start the boundary trace.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Striped Staircase
INSTRUMENTS.description: Browses a live Mandelbrot field and turns escape-depth stripes into discrete steps or sliding musical moments while zoom and traversal reshape timing.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, choose Steps or Slide, then play the depth motion and drag, scroll, or pinch through the live fractal.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Recursive FM
INSTRUMENTS.description: Nests FM operators so every recursion level modulates the next while depth changes are crossfaded.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, then play a MIDI or computer key and adjust depth and modulation amount.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Recursive PM
INSTRUMENTS.description: Folds a carrier through recursive phase operators, adding progressively smaller offsets at deeper levels.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, then play a MIDI or computer key and adjust depth and phase amount.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Chaotic FM
INSTRUMENTS.description: Sends oscillators through a nonlinear FM cascade with a bounded shaping stage between levels.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, then play a MIDI or computer key and shape the cascade depth.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Chaotic PM
INSTRUMENTS.description: Applies nonlinear shaping at each recursive phase-modulation level, with smooth and raw comparison modes.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, then play a MIDI or computer key and compare smooth and raw modes.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Cascading FM
INSTRUMENTS.description: Chains sine oscillators across rising, equal, or falling base frequencies, each one frequency-modulating the next with tapered depth.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, then adjust the stage count, cascade ratio, modulation depth, and depth taper.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Cascading PM
INSTRUMENTS.description: Chains sine operators across rising, equal, or falling base frequencies, with every stage offsetting the next stage's phase in radians.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, then adjust the stage count, cascade ratio, phase index, and index taper.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Weierstrass
INSTRUMENTS.description: Sums exponentially spaced oscillators as a waveform or uses the same fractal bank for FM and phase modulation.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, choose Wave, FM, or Phase, then adjust the oscillator bank.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Fabric Filter
INSTRUMENTS.description: Sends correlated colored noise through interacting two-dimensional wave fields, a Shepard-wrapped Q/FFT lattice, and a visible damped mass-spring frequency fabric shaped by direct grabs and user-triggered propagation.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, choose a preset and sculptor, then grab or pluck the fabric. There are no hidden audio-only LFOs, drifts, motors, or automatic plucks: the direct grab override ends on release, and only visibly moving fabric and user-triggered waves continue moving the spectral controls while normal audio tails decay.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Playhead Paint
INSTRUMENTS.description: Turns freehand pointer strokes into playable sound gestures, mapping position, color, and pen size to pitch and timbre while mirrored axes create polyphonic reflections.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, choose X and Y mappings and a pen, then draw; release to end the note or loop the recorded path.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Boidzoid
INSTRUMENTS.description: Makes autonomous arrow playheads into continuous sine voices: height sweeps frequency without note divisions, horizontal position sets stereo, and speed breathes the level.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, let the arrows drift, then drag the open surface to steer the sine field.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Puggler the Punk Rock Jugger
INSTRUMENTS.description: Turns up to ten objects into a thrashing punk band at up to 1,200 beats/minute. Puggler, Roxy, and Moss pass props, catch audience lobs, and throw them back; catches strike recorded drums and airborne paths bend riffs on a filthy punk stage.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Enable Audio. Fixed clickable keys control each rider: WASD for Puggler, IJKL for Roxy, numpad for Moss. Drag anyone. Pause holds new juggling throws while riders and the crowd stay active.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Vector Flight
INSTRUMENTS.description: Keeps a wireframe ship centered inside a full 360-degree star field, mapping a circular listening contour, azimuth, proximity, radial velocity, and tangential motion directly into continuous voices, free-pitch flybys, or triggers without a scale grid.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, choose Continuous, Notes, or Triggers, drag around the ship to rotate the physics mapping, then raise the throttle until points become hyperspace rays and full-circle plaid.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Gesturama
INSTRUMENTS.description: Turns live motion into painted drums, continuously shaped resonant pads, recorded microphone samples, or a Karplus–Strong video harp.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Start the camera, choose a preset, then move through the grid or strings; use the pointer only to paint new sound zones.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Wheel of Organs
INSTRUMENTS.description: Grows every typed letter into its own morphable glottal mouth on a quiet one-shot wheel, sounding wet nasal and slime cavities only when each organ crosses the fixed three-o'clock reader.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, set the letter wheel, and spin; it accelerates, coasts, and brakes before the final organ sustains and fades, then unlocks for another spin.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Feral Fairy Ferris Ferry
INSTRUMENTS.description: Carries an audible Level 1 contour through nested moving shapes whose inherited positions control pitch, amplitude modulation, delay time, and feedback.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, start the Ferris transport, then assign shapes and Pass, Modulator, or Delay processing to the higher levels.

INSTRUMENTS.label: FM Drums
INSTRUMENTS.description: Edits the sixteen-voice FM and shaped-noise percussion bank used by the drum machines.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio or MIDI, hit a pad, then edit and save its synthesized voice.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Rattlesnake
INSTRUMENTS.description: Maps frequency onto one continuous body with four Rattlesnake models plus a Karplus Strong model whose four complete presets morph across the snake.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, choose a sound model, then drag across the spectrum or silently reposition its dotted morph boundaries.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Karplus Strong
INSTRUMENTS.description: Plucks noise or impulse excitation into a tunable feedback-delay model with spectral loss, polarity, nonlinearity, modulation, pickup, body, and sympathetic-string controls.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, choose a string or preset, then click or drag across the stage to pluck and strum.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Karplus Carpet
INSTRUMENTS.description: Turns a dense two-dimensional surface of close areas into freshly synthesized Karplus attacks with adjustable one-shot amplitude ADSR, two sound-variety banks, deterministic cell color, and coupled resonators across a tunable microtonal pitch field, without loading sample grains.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Press and drag across the surface: each newly crossed area sounds once per gesture, while moving inside an area or holding still stays silent.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Surround for Safety
INSTRUMENTS.description: Places synth or imported audio inside 7:4:1, 4:1, eight-speaker circle, eight-speaker cube, and two-to-thirty-two-channel custom arrays, with calibrated speaker tests and synchronized channel-stem capture.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, choose an array, then test a numbered speaker, move the coral source, load an audio file, or record the virtual outputs as mono WAV stems.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Sample Drums
INSTRUMENTS.description: Edits a sixteen-slot 808/909-style sample bank that can also replace the Lattice Drum Machine synth bank.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio or MIDI, hit a pad, then load or trim samples in the selected slot.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Dentaphone
INSTRUMENTS.description: Turns 32 individually playable upper and lower teeth into a two-layer dental marimba driven by a sample-free AudioWorklet physical model, editable damped modes, spatial excitation, and modal JSON exchange.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio and tap, drag, brush, or chomp the teeth; choose a pitch distribution, then reshape the shared wood, glass, steel, ceramic, bronze, or imported modal body.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Automatapoeia
INSTRUMENTS.description: Shows exact, live-switchable binary evolution across all 256 elementary rules and 64 radius-2 totalistic codes, with explicit boundaries and measurable shape contours.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Change family, rule or code, and boundary without restarting, then sculpt the next rows through finite mono physical, FM/PM, additive, wavefold, or resonant-air voices with swing and ADSR.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Sorting
INSTRUMENTS.description: Runs five sorting algorithms on the same shuffle and maps comparisons, swaps, and writes to sound.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Choose an algorithm, randomize the values, then press Play to hear each operation.

INSTRUMENTS.label: DJ Dijkstra
INSTRUMENTS.description: Spreads a weighted search frontier across a grid and maps node distance, weight, and position into a spatial path score.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, rewire the graph, then play or scrub the frontier.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Wave Pool
INSTRUMENTS.description: Couples piston paddles or pneumatic caissons to a slow gravity-wave clock, then makes breaking spray, entrained bubbles, wet boundary slaps, structural modes, and aerated whirlpools into four interlocking sample-free rhythm lanes.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, run the four-lane sequence, then tap the pool or use keys 1–4 while changing water depth, wave height, bubble radius, wall system, and receiver position.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Penrose Tilings
INSTRUMENTS.description: Moves five exact Penrose presentations behind one fixed reader: edge paths sustain sine voices, while new physical intersections trigger FM percussion.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Choose a presentation and local window, then follow the visible signal net and next-edge targets as the tiling moves; angle shear keeps shared edges sealed while clearly leaving canonical geometry.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Yoyodyne
INSTRUMENTS.description: Sonifies one spinning yo-yo and its constrained string: length and tension bend pitch, travel shapes the voice, and four hand-driven routines trace distinct phrases.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, choose a trick and Perform, or Throw once and drag the hand. Tug excites the string; Catch binds the yo-yo back to the performer.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Hanoi Carillon
INSTRUMENTS.description: Rings every legal Towers of Hanoi transfer as a metallic voice whose pitch follows disk size and pan follows the peg.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, choose the disk count, then play the recursive transfer sequence.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Alpha-Beta Minimax
INSTRUMENTS.description: Turns minimax evaluations into tense calls and answers while alpha-beta pruning cuts branches with percussive noise.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, reseed the contest, then play or scrub the search tree.

INSTRUMENTS.label: N-Queens Backtracker
INSTRUMENTS.description: Builds harmony from valid queen placements, noise from conflicts, and falling gestures from backtracking.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, shuffle the columns, then play the board search.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Euclidean Pulse
INSTRUMENTS.description: Turns Euclidean remainders into descending bass and each exact quotient into a repeated rhythmic pulse cell.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, choose a new ratio, then play or scrub its division chain.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Alien Larynx
INSTRUMENTS.description: Keeps the recognizable Throatazoid voice beneath five optional systems for coupled folds, true-scale propagation, mouth genomes, robot glands, and wormhole routing.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Start with every alien system bypassed, turn on audio, then bring the five mutations online one at a time or return instantly to the anchored voice.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Hyper-Syrinx
INSTRUMENTS.description: Multiplies breaths, membranes, labia, tracheas, tracts, mouths, and lips into a patchable polyphonic physical-voice laboratory.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, duplicate or remove organ modules, choose how they share signals, then hold Breath while reshaping the combined voice.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Morphynx
INSTRUMENTS.description: Crossfades persistent Syrinx and larynx models while multiple physical voices, tongue constrictions, nasal resonances, microphone formants, and letter-key mutations reshape the tract.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Choose an animal and voice, move the Syrinx–Larynx morph, then play a call or hold A–Z; add voices, tongues, or nasal cavities to hear the anatomy branch out.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Escher
INSTRUMENTS.description: Builds original procedural motifs on Euclidean wallpaper groups, similarity recursions, and exact Poincaré-disk reflection tilings whose rendered contours become the playhead paths.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Tap a shape, then follow its literal outline, real shared-border neighbors, or matching pattern family; smaller measured contours naturally recur faster.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Plasma Ball
INSTRUMENTS.description: Fires quiet, intermittent synth-static through branching paths across the near and far surfaces of a three-dimensional glass globe.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, then move or touch the glass to gather some discharges while the rest keep searching the globe.

INSTRUMENTS.label: SIMD Resonator
INSTRUMENTS.description: Turns one strike into a 128-mode resonant body whose material, position, hardness, tuning, decay, and inharmonic spread remain directly playable while WebAssembly SIMD accelerates the parallel modes.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on Audio, choose a material, then tap or drag the body. Microphone input can excite the same resonator.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Order Tones
INSTRUMENTS.description: Turns modular repetition and an inverse-QFT model into a probability comb used to estimate order and factors.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, choose a preset, then run shots and listen to the probability peaks.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Morphazoidical
INSTRUMENTS.description: Shows the live form, contact, reader, and event data available for geometry-to-sound mappings.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, choose a form and reader, then drag the stage and inspect its live values.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Bell Square
INSTRUMENTS.description: Simulates two atoms with a controlled collision phase and sonifies correlated measurements along chosen axes.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, choose measurement axes, then run repeated shots.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Entanglement Dance
INSTRUMENTS.description: Hears quantum entanglement as a slowed-down square dance — two qubits precess together or in opposition based on their Bell state.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, press play, then try each Bell state and listen for correlated or anti-correlated melodic motion.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Quantum Square Dance
INSTRUMENTS.description: Runs an exact classical simulation of controlled spin exchange in paired atoms and sonifies the evolving joint state, phase, and correlations.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, then play or scrub the exchange dance and compare its paired-atom scenes.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Annealogue
INSTRUMENTS.description: Moves eight three-qubit states through an anneal, mapping energy, probability, and phase to a cube and choir.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, choose a problem preset, then run or scrub the anneal.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Gravity Walk
INSTRUMENTS.description: Moves a bead along a polygon, star, or circle and maps height, speed, and impacts to sound.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, choose a path, then release the bead or change gravity.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Ricochet
INSTRUMENTS.description: Bounces balls through editable arenas where wall angle controls pitch and impact speed controls level.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, choose an arena, then launch balls and move its walls.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Rigidity
INSTRUMENTS.description: Loads pinned bar-and-joint structures under gravity to reveal which constraints hold, flex, or fail.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, choose a structure, then apply load or move a joint.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Rolling Measure
INSTRUMENTS.description: Rolls regular polygons vertex to vertex while centroid lift, contact changes, and impact loss shape the sound.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, choose a polygon, then start rolling and adjust the surface.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Falling Forms
INSTRUMENTS.description: Drops rigid forms into a stage and maps impacts, rotation, friction, and settling to sound.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, choose a form, then drop copies into the stage.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Charge Garden
INSTRUMENTS.description: Combines positive and negative charges in a softened field with visible tracers and equipotential lines.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, place or drag charges, then release tracers into the field.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Packing Pressure
INSTRUMENTS.description: Compresses falling disks into a contact network and maps force, density, coordination, and jams to sound.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, add disks, then lower the press or change their packing.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Geodesic Drift
INSTRUMENTS.description: Compares nearby straightest paths on a plane, cylinder, sphere, and torus as their separation evolves.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, choose a surface, then launch nearby paths and vary their starting angle.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Kinetic Hull
INSTRUMENTS.description: Recomputes a convex hull and Delaunay edges around moving points; boundary changes and edge flips trigger sound.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, add or move points, then start their motion.

INSTRUMENTS.label: RISSET-MOIRE
INSTRUMENTS.description: Crosses rising and falling Shepard lattices so weighted line intersections emphasize audible coincidences.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, start both layers, then change their angles and glissando rates.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Chladni Plate
INSTRUMENTS.description: Draws standing-wave nodal curves on a square plate and uses mode and strike position to shape its partials.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, choose a plate mode, then click or drag a strike point.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Spring Choir
INSTRUMENTS.description: Simulates a coupled mass-spring chain and turns its normal modes into a quiet oscillator choir.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, pull a mass, then release it and change the coupling.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Gear Ratio Drums
INSTRUMENTS.description: Rotates two meshed cogs at tooth-locked rates so contacts become a gear-ratio polyrhythm.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, choose tooth counts, then start the gears and change their speed.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Prime Sieve
INSTRUMENTS.description: Runs the sieve of Eratosthenes, turning prime discoveries into a rising melody and eliminations into ticks.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, reset the grid, then run or step through the sieve.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Lissajous Orbits
INSTRUMENTS.description: Uses one integer ratio for both a closed Lissajous curve and its two-oscillator musical interval.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, choose an axis ratio, then change phase and speed.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Pendulum Wave
INSTRUMENTS.description: Sets neighboring pendulums to related periods so they drift apart, form waves, and reunite.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, release the pendulums, then change their count or period spread.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Double Pendulum
INSTRUMENTS.description: Releases two nearly identical double pendulums and widens an interval as their chaotic paths diverge.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, set a small starting difference, then release both pendulums.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Reaction-Diffusion
INSTRUMENTS.description: Evolves a Gray-Scott chemical field through spots, bands, and splits that control a small sound field.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, choose a reaction preset, then seed or paint the field.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Atomic Orbitals
INSTRUMENTS.description: Draws signed planar slices of hydrogen orbitals and maps quantum numbers and nodes to a harmonic bank.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, choose quantum numbers, then move through the orbital slice.

INSTRUMENTS.label: DNA Translator
INSTRUMENTS.description: Scans editable DNA through four base pitches and adds a tone for each completed amino-acid codon.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, edit or randomize the strand, then start the scanner.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Neural Pulse
INSTRUMENTS.description: Sends four inputs through a fixed weighted network and triggers sound as activity crosses each layer.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, change the four inputs, then send a pulse through the network.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Fourier Epicycles
INSTRUMENTS.description: Chains rotating harmonic vectors into classic waveforms, with every visible vector acting as an audible partial.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, choose a waveform, then change the number of epicycles.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Gravity Lens
INSTRUMENTS.description: Uses an idealized gravitational lens to split one source into two apparent images and a paired interval.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, move the source or lens, then compare image position, level, and delay.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Cantor Lock
INSTRUMENTS.description: Searches for a finite signal inside matching Cantor-shaped position and frequency masks, mapping addresses to pitch and pulse while retained energy and leakage divide a glass-and-amber ensemble.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, compare an interval with Cantor masks, then tighten the trap and listen to retained energy separate from leakage.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Escape Dust
INSTRUMENTS.description: Compares classical survivors with a leaking finite wave in an open triadic baker map: phase-space position writes melody and pan, survival orchestrates the chord, and escape flux strikes its accents.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, release a packet, then step or play the map while escaped points and wave energy enter the flux monitor.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Linebreaker
INSTRUMENTS.description: Probes crossed lines, a Sierpiński carpet, and Cantor dust while occupied runs sustain organ rails, gaps fracture the phrase, and two-dimensional Fourier peaks orchestrate the harmony.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Turn on audio, rotate the line probe across each structure, then compare its sampled gaps with the two-dimensional Fourier pattern.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Tempo Tantrum
INSTRUMENTS.description: Three continuously evolving phase oscillators lock to a driving pulse, slip outside the locking range, and recover after a nudge; their own crossings trigger the notes.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Enable Audio and Play, then nudge a bead or drag it outward to detune it. Compare strong coupling with a released drive.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Tape Worm
INSTRUMENTS.description: One playback head crosses between two intact recordings at movable splices, with file and microphone capture, varispeed, and a bypass for original loops.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Enable Audio and Play to hear the demo, then drag a splice or click a tape to reposition the reader. Recording replaces only the selected tape.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Loop Soup
INSTRUMENTS.description: Three persistent loops mix stored audio, a local demo ingredient, or microphone input with bounded spill between bowls, exact hold, overdubbing, and selective erasure.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Enable Audio and Play, select a bowl, and compare Hold with Overdub. Turn on the erase brush to remove sound from a region of tape.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Habit Habitat
INSTRUMENTS.description: Manual node visits teach a bounded transition network; seeded weighted recall plays those tendencies without reinforcing its own playback.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Enable Audio, choose Teach, and tap numbered nodes. Switch to Recall and Play to hear the learned routes; save a memory in this browser.

INSTRUMENTS.label: Hollowphonic
INSTRUMENTS.description: Three damped, coupled delay-line resonators reshape noise, a drone, or microphone input; dragging cavity depth retunes resonances and direct strikes excite the same chambers.
INSTRUMENTS.start: Enable Audio and Play, drag a chamber deeper, or strike it directly. Compare bypass and damping while the source remains unchanged.

tools.label: Shape
tools.description: Scans a 2D contour with moving points, lines, or rays; each geometric contact shapes pitch, pan, level, and timbre.
tools.start: Turn on audio, choose a reader, then move the contour or play a MIDI or computer key.

tools.label: Solid
tools.description: Cuts a moving 3D wireframe with a plane; every wire-plane intersection becomes a voice.
tools.start: Turn on audio, choose a solid, then rotate it or move the cutting plane.

tools.label: Möbius
tools.description: Sweeps a two-dimensional plane through a half-twisted Möbius band, or runs a 16-station, two-lap counterpoint weave whose hocketed subject gains an offbeat answer and inverts on the shadow lap.
tools.start: Choose Plane slice for playable intersection curves, or Counterpoint weave for the perpendicular A–B crossbar, mirrored pitch traces, and forward-only two-lap phrase.

tools.label: Klein Bottle
tools.description: Sweeps a two-dimensional plane through a figure-eight Klein bottle immersion while keeping coincident sheets separate in the parameter mesh.
tools.start: Turn on Audio, press Play or drag the 2D head, then tilt its plane and reshape the immersion while its glowing slice curves remain the score.

tools.label: Hyper
tools.description: Cuts a rotating 4D wireframe with a W hyperplane and sonifies the crossing edges.
tools.start: Turn on audio, choose a 4D form, then move the W reader or start rotation.

tools.label: Graph Synth
tools.description: Sends inherited-pitch note pulses through editable directed graphs; edge length sets time, route turns set intervals, and cycle-closing edges create quieter, darker repeats.
tools.start: Turn on audio, choose or generate a graph, then send one note or run the pulse clock while dragging nodes and switching routes.

tools.label: Shapes
tools.description: A self-contained Polygon, Polyhedra, and Hyperpolyhedra instrument with one canvas, one shared transport, and dimension-aware form and rotation controls.
tools.start: Choose 2D, 3D, or 4D, then play the same running form continuously, as notes, or as triggers from the responsive Twin Rack panel.

tools.label: L-Systems
tools.description: A self-contained L-system instrument with one canvas, shared grammar controls, and Continuous, Notes, Triggers, and Mic playing modes.
tools.start: Choose a grammar and mix preset, then keep the same branch traversal running while switching between sustained synth, note events, drum triggers, and live mic delay.

tools.label: Graphs
tools.description: A self-contained graph instrument with one editable network and Synth, Drums, and Mic playing modes that share its nodes, routes, motion, and timing.
tools.start: Choose or generate a graph, then reshape and play the same topology while switching between pitched pulses, percussion triggers, and live microphone delay.

tools.label: Tiles
tools.description: A self-contained lattice and spiral instrument with one canvas, shared isohedral tile controls, sustained synth modes, and FM drum trigger modes.
tools.start: Choose Lattice, Lattice Drums, Spiral, or Spiral Drums, then keep the same tile form and reader transport running while switching sound engines.

tools.label: Mazes
tools.description: Carves orthogonal, radial, or hexagonal fields as paired passage-center and wall-outline voices, with a distinct visual and sonic process for each maze algorithm.
tools.start: Choose a field and builder, replay its construction, then optionally trace, tour, or solve the finished topology.

tools.label: Paths
tools.description: Draws Gilbert, Hilbert, Gosper, Dragon, and seeded walking paths as continuous vector scores whose direction, curvature, hierarchy, and position shape sound.
tools.start: Choose a generator, draw it through time, then trace the finished path with one or more sounding heads.

tools.label: Lattice
tools.description: Slides an editable isohedral tiling beneath a reader so every crossed edge becomes a polyphonic synth event.
tools.start: Turn on audio, choose a tiling, then start the motion and move the reader.

tools.label: Spiral
tools.description: Warps an isohedral tiling into log-polar space and scans its radial and spiral edges for sound.
tools.start: Turn on audio, choose a reader, then run or drag the warped lattice.

tools.label: Lattice Drum Machine
tools.description: Turns tiling-reader contacts into drum hits selected and retuned by edge class, orientation, height, and angle.
tools.start: Turn on audio, choose a tiling and bank, then start the lattice motion.

tools.label: Spiral Drum Machine
tools.description: Turns contacts in a log-polar tiling into drum patterns that follow its radial and spiral geometry.
tools.start: Turn on audio, choose a bank and reader, then run the spiral field.

tools.label: Shape Drum Machine
tools.description: Turns contour contacts and corner events into drum hits whose voices change with position, angle, and phase.
tools.start: Turn on audio, choose a reader and drum bank, then move the contour through it.

tools.label: Solid Drum Machine
tools.description: Turns intersections between a cutting plane and a 3D wireframe into a changing drum pattern.
tools.start: Turn on audio, choose a bank, then rotate the solid or move the plane.

tools.label: Hyper Drum Machine
tools.description: Turns 4D hyperplane intersections into drum hits selected by position and four-dimensional rotation.
tools.start: Turn on audio, choose a bank, then move the W reader or start rotation.

tools.label: L-System Drum Machine
tools.description: Walks through recursive branch heads and maps depth, angle, generation, phase, and position to drums.
tools.start: Turn on audio, choose a grammar and drum bank, then generate and play the tree.

tools.label: Graph Drum Machine
tools.description: Propagates percussion triggers through editable directed graphs, mapping node position, degree, route turn, path depth, and cycle pass to a shared sixteen-voice FM drum bank.
tools.start: Turn on audio, choose a topology and drum style, then seed a pulse or run the clock; cyclic routes return later with reduced amplitude and tone.

tools.label: Rattle Snake Skin
tools.description: Paints notes, glissandi, rings, and parameter fields onto a looping time-frequency canvas powered by continuous percussion.
tools.start: Turn on audio, choose a preset and paint tool, draw on the canvas, then start the loop.

tools.label: Rubix Cube Sequencer
tools.description: Offers five mutually exclusive banks: four sample-free drum kits read the two side faces, while 303 Acid reads only the upper face through its Classic or WebGPU engine; hidden stickers stay hard-silent.
tools.start: Choose one bank or preset, then drag the cube or enable Random Twists; in WebGPU 303 mode, sticker row, column, edge, current face, and visibility reshape each acid step.

tools.label: Sliding Puzzle
tools.description: Reads a resizable 2 × 2 through 8 × 8 square or rectangular tile field as either a serial score or Rubix-style parallel rows, with four fixed home-row colors and one moving silent cell.
tools.start: Choose Lines together or One tile, set independent rows and columns, then slide complete lines, rotate the rectangle, scramble, or let Solve unwind the exact move history.

tools.label: Hocket Luigi
tools.description: Distributes one composite rhythm across two, three, or four editable voices, with sourced structural studies, visible gaps and collisions, phase shifts, and direct pulse ownership.
tools.start: Turn on audio, run the loom, then drag or tap pulses between colored rings; keep Preserve composite on to move ownership without changing the combined rhythm.

tools.label: Hyper Rubix
tools.description: Separates five instrument presets—color drums, resonant prisms, bit voices, WebGPU acid, and seed-shell rattles—from three playback views: one selected cell, four view-facing cells, or all 64, 216, or 512 distinct notes in an order-2, order-3, or order-4 tesseract boundary.
tools.start: Turn on audio and Play shape loop, then orbit, Fold W, or make manual quarter-turns: the view chooses the clocked stickers while transformed position, depth, neighbors, fault lines, displacement, and disorder reshape each note without resetting time or adding a separate motion synth.

tools.label: WebGPU 303
tools.description: Streams a WGSL compute-shader acid voice into Web Audio chunks as a separate GPU synthesis instrument.
tools.start: Use a WebGPU-capable browser, turn on Audio, then shape the pattern, partials, filter, and chunk settings.

tools.label: SIMD 303
tools.description: Expands the WebGPU 303 acid model with 512 band-limited partials, harmonic spectrum shaping, per-step expression, chorus, and delay inside a 128-frame AudioWorklet.
tools.start: Turn on Audio, press Play synth, shape the pattern and effects, or save named patches to My presets in this browser.

tools.label: SIMD SYNTH
tools.description: Combines two of eight synthesis models through selectable blend, ring, phase, shaping, filter-routing, modulation, and dual-effects stages in an eight-voice AudioWorklet.
tools.start: Turn on Audio, choose a signal-path preset, play the stage or MIDI keys, then swap sources and processing stages without patching cables.

tools.label: WebGPU Chiptune
tools.description: Translates srtuss's 2015 Shadertoy Chiptune sound shader into a live WGSL score with chip voices, drums, noise, and eight-tap ping-pong echo.
tools.start: Use a WebGPU-capable browser, start the tracker, turn on Audio to hear it, then drag the score to reshape its deterministic seed and pitch range or open the full active-path controls.

tools.label: Jaw Jam
tools.description: Sequences one physical jaw-harp reed through plucks, pitch-inheriting sustains, and exact hard rests while every step can reshape material, mouth vowel, tine pull, breath power, and breath speed.
tools.start: Choose a performance, drag each pluck block vertically for pitch, set its vowel and physical voice, balance PULL with AIR, then run independent pluck and breath clocks at ratios from one breath every three beats through three per beat.

tools.label: GPU Shader Synths
tools.description: Runs four control lanes, six adjustable synthesis models, editable additive ranks, a causal FIR, feed-forward delay taps, and waveshaping across two WGSL compute passes.
tools.start: Use a WebGPU-capable browser, turn on Audio, choose a theme or sequence generator, then draw pitch, pulse, timbre, and model motion directly on the stage.

tools.label: srtuss Master
tools.description: Splits eight Shadertoy Sound programs into 48 selectable source parts while retaining all ten verified translations as exact Original programs.
tools.start: Use a WebGPU-capable browser, start transport and Audio independently, choose a Parts preset or Explode mix, then shape, solo, mute, pan, or retime each voice card.

tools.label: Modular Shader Synth
tools.description: Patches typed synthesis, modulation, shaping, control, and spatial modules into an editable graph that renders stereo audio with WGSL compute shaders.
tools.start: Use a WebGPU-capable browser, select a patch, turn on Audio, then select modules to change their parameters and signal routing.

tools.label: Throatazoid
tools.description: Feeds microphone input, an internal glottis, or both through up to seven editable vocal tracts.
tools.start: Choose the glottis or microphone source, turn on audio, then drag the tongue and tract controls.

tools.label: Pink Trombonazoid
tools.description: Turns a written word into editable phoneme blocks and automation lanes that animate pitch, breath, tongue, lips, nasal coupling, and mutation through a physical vocal tract.
tools.start: Enter a word, turn on audio, press Say word, then reshape its phoneme timing and articulatory automation lanes.

tools.label: Throat Singing
tools.description: Keeps a pressure-driven glottal drone and a tract-selected upper melody inside one 44-section airway, with two constrictions, converging F2/F3 resonances, and optional ventricular-fold period division.
tools.start: Turn on audio, choose a Tuvan style or comparison preset, then retune the drone with A S D F G H J K while selecting harmonics or dragging the tongue and pharynx controls.

tools.label: Syrinx
tools.description: Models mammal folds, paired bird labia, frog membranes, and a rodent jet whistle through species-bounded vocal anatomy.
tools.start: Choose an animal and call, turn on audio, then trigger the gesture or hold Breath while reshaping its biological controls.

tools.label: Tongued Beasts
tools.description: Grafts human, macaque, canine, and avian tongue mechanics onto physical animal voice sources so tongue shape and motion continuously reshape the tract.
tools.start: Turn on audio, choose a host animal and tongue entity, then drag the anatomy or trigger a tongue movement preset.

tools.label: Hybrinx
tools.description: Reveals the native keyframed pressure, pitch, closure, mouth, cavity, roughness, source-split, and bilateral-balance contours that animate physical animal calls through a playable tongue-shaped tract.
tools.start: Turn on audio, choose a host beast and native call, then play or loop it while the live timeline traces every sounding parameter contour beneath the animal.

tools.label: Creaturazoid
tools.kind: Monophonic creature voice and body sequencer
tools.description: Routes 50 gestures—36 animal voices plus 14 procedural hisses, impacts, scrapes, wing sounds, breaths, feeding clicks, and locomotion—through one persistent absolute Hybrinx body.
tools.start: Turn on audio, choose a persistent body and rhythm, then intersperse vocal calls with body percussion; every rectangular step retargets the same airway and body-cavity resonator.

tools.label: Quadruped
tools.description: Keeps species-shaped bodies, including Frog, above a compact sixteen-card motion study; touchdown, load, push, support, lift-off, and landing share one exact global BPM clock with three optional melodic calls.
tools.start: Play Solo, Herd or Trio and edit each animal's foot and call score. Borrow the same gait dictionary and stretch leaps or skids. Change continuous ground material or stair direction for seeded friction and depth color; tempo stays independent.

tools.label: Roach Synth
tools.description: A grounded cockroach scan with 31 playable joints, static poses and 24 varied motions, a body-part mixer, real movement recordings and a crunchy word voice.
tools.start: Turn Audio on, play a held pose or animate it, then mix its legs, shell, wings and voice. Drag a body part, choose a motion, or make a new random motion.

tools.label: Spider Synth
tools.description: A detailed orb-weaver scan with eight articulated legs in a playable web. Leg contacts pluck silk subdivisions, while held poses, a body mixer and a tiny voice shape its sound.
tools.start: Turn Audio on, pluck a strand or animate the spider. Drag its joints, move it across the web, change silk tension, or hold MIDI keys to play temporary poses.

tools.label: Monstrozoid
tools.description: Routes variable lungs, vocal-fold sources, paths, and mouth resonators through continuous pressure, tension, routing, articulation, impact, and resonance contours.
tools.start: Turn on audio and select a call to hear it immediately, or start continuous flow; then edit anatomy counts, route connections, vocal behavior, and modulation contours.

tools.label: Blowhole
tools.description: Separates delphinid phonic lips, the sperm whale's right-sided spermaceti pathway, and the coupled U-fold/cricoid-cushion source of baleen-whale song while the external blowhole remains a valve rather than the underwater sound source.
tools.start: Turn on audio, choose a dolphin or whale call, then play its visible gesture or hold pressure while dragging the paired source, air sac, and radiator anatomy.

tools.label: Jaw Harp
tools.description: Couples a plucked cantilever reed to an interactive mouth cavity so one fixed reed fundamental excites harmonics selected by the tongue, jaw, lips, and cavity.
tools.start: Turn on audio, choose a harp and vowel preset, then pull and release the copper trigger or press Space to pluck.

tools.label: Harmonicazoid
tools.description: Models a three-octave, ten-hole diatonic harmonica as paired blow and draw reeds, with independent keys and reed bodies, one- to five-hole apertures, bends, tongue blocks, a moving hand-cavity resonance, and signed blues breath rhythms.
tools.start: Turn on audio, choose Midnight Growl or another performance, then hold Blow or Draw; pull either lip-window edge, reshape the tongue and bend, sweep the hand cup, or move Breath Shift from pristine to sloppy.

tools.label: Julie Saw
tools.description: Localizes a long singing mode at the inflection of an S-curved steel blade, then couples bow pressure, signed speed, rosin, and moving contact through a velocity-weakening stick–slip junction.
tools.start: Turn on audio, drag Julie's pink flex hand to bend and curl the blade, then drag the amber bow across its moving sweet spot. Lift to ring, or explore sourced bow pulses, vibrato, glides, mallets, edge pluck, scrape, and choke.

tools.label: Hiccup Head
tools.description: Moves a softly translucent, step-shifting pastel-rainbow checkerboard polka-dot goofball face and one persistent Pink Trombone–lineage oral waveguide between fifty-two exclusive gestures, including sustained alveolar ZZZZ, a vibrato-rich EH-YEAH vowel carousel, moving WAOW, arched WHOOP, pitched DOO-DOO, held lateral LLLL, long RRRR, alternating L-R-L-R, LA-LA-LA, four-place KLIK-KLAK clicks, low PURR, warm HUFF, short HIC!, full HICCUP!, EEF! breaths, a wet double KISS, bidirectional BRUSH tooth gliss, mouth KSH snare, longer cheek toms, BRRAP, resonant face claps, open-throat and rough voices, grunt, moan, PB-PB, a wet pull-out tongue, missing-incisor FWEE, and twelve pitched dead-wood teeth.
tools.start: Tap any of fifty-two feature-clear sound dots, the whistle gap, or twelve separately pitched crooked teeth. Choose or mutate among seven contrasting physical sound banks; every bank retunes the same monophonic mouth and auditions its result. KISS leaves a fading lip print at a changing face position, BRUSH sends a visible toothbrush up and down while sweeping both directions across the wood-toned teeth, and blue slap mitts appear only while SLAP or SMACK is dragged. Pull either horizontal-tethered ear for stereo width, and drag each straight side-hair tip in two dimensions—length sets echo amount while angle sets that side's delay time. Matched circular eyes move inward for bright plate reverb, outward for a dark cathedral, and downward to thicken the room; centered open eyes are dry. Use two thick eyebrows as a cyclic sequence-amplitude contour. The large glossy #FF0000 circular nose controls the nasal branch, while the oval green, translucent-striped lips become thinner as the mouth opens. Persistent Delay, Reverb, Nasal, and Stereo switches and live amounts stay put through preset changes, mutation, and reset. Sequence one gesture per column at any length from 1 through 64 steps and up to 520 BPM, then edit or mutate one to eight sequential voice characters—including direct vibrato rate and depth—without layering mouths.

tools.label: Digestazoid
tools.description: Couples a compliant stomach, peristaltic intestinal and colon chambers, gas, bile-like liquid, viscous sludge, a finite bubble-cloud model, and pressure-driven upper and lower tissue valves into one persistent wet body. Bubble events pass through dirty nucleation, submerged inverse-size rings, neck pinch, surface rupture, viscous glugs, and shared low abdominal modes.
tools.start: Turn on audio, push and prod the cutaway organs, hold Inflate or Deflate, pinch and release a valve, pull the lower rubber outlet, or play growl, clustered burble, bubble rupture, slosh, burp, sludge burple, and short or sustained fart gestures.

tools.label: Mouthophones
tools.description: Mouthophones compares nineteen breath-driven and mouth-resonated instruments through six physical source topologies, from quill-driven strings and bidirectional free reeds to lip reeds, edge-tone flutes, lamellophones, and mouth bows.
tools.start: Choose an instrument by evidence tier, turn on audio, then hold inhale or exhale; for hand-driven strings, pluck, rub, or bow against a linked breath rhythm.

tools.label: Spelling Synthesizer
tools.description: Sounds each typed letter through the Bellazoid tract, sustained KAL phone samples, or the twenty-band Voxazoid vocoder while typing rhythm shapes the voice.
tools.start: Begin typing, choose an engine and personality, then adjust rhythm dynamics and the vowel-pair delay.

tools.label: Vocalzoid
tools.description: Turns one written word into editable pitched notes, sustained vowel bodies, and overlapped phoneme joins using bundled open sample voices or a local UTAU bank.
tools.start: Turn on audio, drag the syllable notes into a melody, choose KAL16 or one of eight bundled open demo voices, then press Sing word; extracted UTAU folders can be imported locally.

tools.label: Lumber Loops
tools.description: Records microphone loops as playable rings with pitch handles, filters, direction, pan, mute, solo, and shared delay.
tools.start: Allow microphone access, record a first ring, then drag its playheads and pitch handles.

tools.label: L-system Delay
tools.description: Runs live microphone audio through an L-system tree where branches become delays and turns become pitch shifts.
tools.start: Allow microphone access, start input, then change the grammar or branch timing.

tools.label: Graph Delay
tools.description: Routes live microphone audio through a generated delay graph with switchable paths, pitch shifts, and feedback.
tools.start: Allow microphone access, choose a graph preset, then start input and open or close routes.

tools.label: Micromorph
tools.description: Streams microphone audio and sample-clocked performance controls to an optional local diffusion model, while five visible membranes expose the path from source to imaginary descendant.
tools.start: Use headphones, turn on the microphone, move Ancestor distance through the five derivation stages, then connect an MGA Stream v1 model host for neural audio; without one, the page identifies its bounded rehearsal DSP honestly.

tools.label: Shepard–Risset
tools.description: Builds the illusion of endlessly rising or falling pitch from overlapping octave layers.
tools.start: Turn on audio, choose a direction or preset, then adjust speed, density, and range.

tools.label: Slippery Resynthesis
tools.description: Tracks microphone or local-file audio across logarithmic FFT bands, then rebuilds it through endlessly slipping Shepard glissando banks with adaptive consonant excitation.
tools.start: Choose Mic or File, turn on audio, then shape the glide, transpose, spectral tilt, carrier color, consonant detail, stereo spread, and dry/slip mix.

tools.label: Drum Roll Please!
tools.description: Translates the Shepard–Risset illusion into overlapping tempo octaves whose struck voices morph from kick through tom, hand drum, and air.
tools.start: Choose a direction and tempo glissando, then optionally make pitch follow the endlessly changing rhythm rate.

tools.label: Ouroborousel
tools.description: Builds an endless roll from higher-note chunks, Ouroboros drum bodies, or both, carrying octave-related pulses through the rhythm–pitch fusion threshold.
tools.start: Choose Notes, Ouroboros Drums, or Notes + Drums, start the carousel, and shape its direction, roll rate, bank width, and shared rhythm-to-pitch fusion; Notes and Combo also expose note-chunk controls.

tools.label: Ourorourobouroboros
tools.description: Purple-and-blue octave rings carry slow drum or note rhythms into pitch, then slower phase-locked gates carve silences into the high spectrum so the next rhythm seems to emerge from inside it.
tools.start: Choose Notes, Drums, or Layered, add or remove Shepard rings, then shape the pitch threshold, note-lift/nested distance, interruption reach, silence depth, and rhythm-to-sustain audio mix.

tools.label: Ouroboros
tools.description: Strikes a Rattlesnake-style drum through octave-related Shepard bodies whose pitch keeps rising or falling while the audible register appears never to leave.
tools.start: Turn on audio, choose Rise or Fall, then balance glissando speed, hit rate, octave-bank width, and the kick-to-air timbre morph.

tools.label: Ouroboros Borealis
tools.description: Crosses an endless Shepard pitch bank with an endless Risset rhythm bank, giving one Rattlesnake percussion body independent illusory pitch and tempo motion.
tools.start: Start the dual playheads, send pitch and rhythm together or in opposite directions, then reshape their intervals, phase, coupling, ranges, and timbre.

tools.label: Sandy Syrup Delay
tools.description: Processes microphone or file audio with staggered grains that can hold their rates or glide together.
tools.start: Choose microphone or a file, start the source, then move between Sand and Syrup behavior.

tools.label: Candy Coil Delay
tools.description: Uses staggered centered-hump delay heads that pass below, through, and above the source pitch.
tools.start: Choose microphone or a file, start the source, then tap a range or lock its reciprocal relationship with head speed.

tools.label: L-System
tools.description: Expands turtle grammars into branching scores whose recursion, turns, taper, and timing shape a voice tree.
tools.start: Turn on audio, select a grammar, generate the tree, then play its branch traversal.

tools.label: Recursion
tools.description: Runs noise, impulses, microphone capture, or a file through the recursive Fuzzy Donut signal process.
tools.start: Choose a source, turn on audio, then raise the recursion depth and switch visual views.

tools.label: Enveloper
tools.description: Embeds three child envelopes inside one parent envelope, then divides them into nine FM notes with editable pitch and index contours; each ancestor segment's slope becomes inherited pitch glide.
tools.start: Turn on audio and start the tree clock, drag parent and child nodes to reshape time, level, and inherited bend, then set each leaf's base sound and its two modulation contours.

tools.label: Julia
tools.description: Traces a Julia-set boundary and maps left and right turns to cyclic Shepard pitch.
tools.start: Turn on audio, choose or drag the Julia parameter, then start the boundary trace.

tools.label: Striped Staircase
tools.description: Browses a live Mandelbrot field and turns escape-depth stripes into discrete steps or sliding musical moments while zoom and traversal reshape timing.
tools.start: Turn on audio, choose Steps or Slide, then play the depth motion and drag, scroll, or pinch through the live fractal.

tools.label: Recursive FM
tools.description: Nests FM operators so every recursion level modulates the next while depth changes are crossfaded.
tools.start: Turn on audio, then play a MIDI or computer key and adjust depth and modulation amount.

tools.label: Recursive PM
tools.description: Folds a carrier through recursive phase operators, adding progressively smaller offsets at deeper levels.
tools.start: Turn on audio, then play a MIDI or computer key and adjust depth and phase amount.

tools.label: Chaotic FM
tools.description: Sends oscillators through a nonlinear FM cascade with a bounded shaping stage between levels.
tools.start: Turn on audio, then play a MIDI or computer key and shape the cascade depth.

tools.label: Chaotic PM
